nodes.description: Disease variants are de novo and almost all missense; one canonical splice variant is reported. Eleven of thirteen distinct variants lie in exon 4 and two in exon 3, in an evolutionarily conserved alpha helix (helix 2) that, with the previously known Rag-binding helix 1, is necessary and sufficient for TFE3 to bind the Rag GTPases. Structure prediction places the patient-mutated residues at the TFE3-RagA interface, and the missense variants abolish Rag GTPase binding.

nodes.description: When nutrients are present, active Rag GTPases bind TFE3 at the lysosomal surface. Rag binding secludes TFE3 in the cytoplasm and activates a conserved phospho-degron that leads to CUL1-beta-TrCP ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. Variants that cannot bind the Rag GTPases escape both controls, leaving TFE3 constitutively stable.

This is the proposed link between the variants and the neurodevelopmental phenotype; it has not been tested in human neural tissue or in an animal model carrying a patient variant.
